verdicts.rewritten_summary: Human Rights Watch (29 Oct 2025) reports a leaked draft of Türkiye's omnibus '11th Judicial Package' (national framework; the record's national-frame claim on the draft rests on this) that would amend the penal code to criminalise conduct deemed contrary to biological sex and general morality and its promotion with up to three years' prison, and participation in same-sex engagement or marriage ceremonies with up to four years, and would amend civil code article 40 to raise the minimum age for gender-affirming care including surgery from 18 to 25 with mandatory permanent infertility and repeated evaluations at government-approved hospitals. Healthcare professionals performing deemed-illegal interventions would face fines and up to seven years' prison and trans people receiving such care up to three years, with courts able to order pretrial detention; fifteen Turkish LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association opposed the draft, and HRW warns it would force treatment into unregulated underground settings.
verdicts.note: national-framework source; rule-5 retention: record text makes claims this source supports and no region-specific source covers them

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Kaos GL's report on 2025 ('A Major Siege against LGBTI+ People in 2025: Hostility Turned into State Policy'; national framework, backing the record's national-frame claims) finds hostility toward LGBTI+ people became explicit state policy: for the first time in many years an LGBTI+ association was closed and criminal cases were opened against 11 of its members for human rights advocacy. It documents six right-to-life violations, three recorded as hate-motivated killings with trans people the most affected, 89 torture/ill-treatment violations, and 313 violations of the right to liberty in 2025 — roughly two and a half times the previous year — citing detentions, arrests and criminal cases against Pride participants as main reasons.
